scope: One locked production-off 0x2F/0x2D read-only candidate execution followed by one exact restore to the captured COMP-REQ-260 application bytes.
PROVEN: COMP-REQ-260 captured two independent 524288-byte application reads with identical raw SHA-256 223F6E... and a valid Cortex-M vector table, then proved the same normal application booted.
The locked candidate HEX and ELF remain byte-identical to the prior default-off build; this Goal does not rebuild them from the concurrently changing upper-layer tree.

The prior static audit proved all controller-side checks except the superseded missing E199 restore file: early return before normal panel init, only 0x2F/0x2D reads, three groups, bounded lengths, forbidden commands absent and GPIO restoration.
The decoder and parser already encode chip ID, busy, consistency, nontrivial payload, VCOM, 0x37 B..F, F6 Mode2 and waveform-version evidence.
The restore identity can now be tested directly by uploading 0x80000 bytes after programmer write/verify and comparing every byte to backup-a.
INFERENCE: The captured raw baseline is a stronger future restore identity than the lost E199 Intel HEX filename/hash because it is the exact pre-run byte range on the board; it still does not reproduce the E199 file container.

A successful candidate parser result followed by exact raw restore and normal boot is sufficient for the bounded controller-state evidence claim, but not for any display waveform or physical residue claim.

The existing candidate may leave the display visually unchanged because it issues no refresh or panel reset; MCU programming and restored normal boot can still produce existing application display behavior.
UNKNOWN: The actual 0x2F and 0x2D values remain unknown until the sole candidate execution.
The physical panel's waveform/temperature binding and RAM ping-pong semantics remain unknown even if F6 is read.
Physical screen appearance during candidate/restore MCU resets is outside this machine-only Goal.
RISK: Any candidate attempt requires the finally restore path even when flashing, serial capture or controller parsing fails.
A restore write/verify/upload mismatch or missing normal boot leaves application recovery unproven and requires immediate human escalation without a second write, reset or connection.
Changing or rebuilding the candidate would invalidate the locked static evidence and is forbidden.
Publishing raw application binaries in docs or Git would violate the private-baseline boundary.

ADMISSION.pre_hardware: Revalidate backup-a and backup-b length/hash/bytes/vector, candidate hash, static/host/parser gates, serial and both locks before the first write.
ADMISSION.candidate: At most one programmer process/write of locked 52D79C... candidate after serial ready.
ADMISSION.controller: Exactly three 0x2F/1-byte plus 0x2D/11-byte groups; parser determines valid or invalid without retry.
ADMISSION.restore: Once candidate is attempted, exactly one programmer process with one backup-a write at 0x08000000, verify, one 0x80000 upload to private restore-verify.bin and one reset; uploaded bytes must equal baseline.
ADMISSION.normal_resume: One bounded post-restore serial window with normal boot and ready, and no diagnostic residue, panel error or hardfault.

non_goals: Rebuild candidate or reconstruct E199 Intel HEX
Read 0x41, 0x27, panel RAM, wireless stack, option bytes, keys, OTP or memory above the application baseline
Issue panel refresh, hard reset, initialization, high voltage, RAM/LUT/OTP/0x37 write or forbidden SSD1681 command
Perform visual, residue, White/Black, rail, temperature, animation, waveform, production, touch or BLE work
